author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
description:
Pup named Roo, who ran away from home, was found curled up next to rail track – and was ‘thrilled’ to be rescued

A two-year-old pitbull who ran away from home braved two days in a dim San Francisco railway tunnel before being rescued.

Caltrain operators spotted the pup named Roo on his first day in the tunnel. Looking at the dog’s unmoving body, they had assumed he had been fatally struck by a train, according to a recent social media post from the San Francisco animal care and control shelter.

Continue reading...
title: San Francisco pitbull rescued after two days trapped in railway tunnel

author: Josh Halliday North of England editor
description:
Bev Craig succeeds Andy Burnham and wins back support in areas where Reform made gains in May

Labour has stormed to a decisive victory in the Greater Manchester mayoral byelection, seizing back areas that recently fell to Reform UK and the Greens.

Labour’s Bev Craig, the Manchester city council leader, will now succeed Andy Burnham and hold one of the most powerful political positions outside Westminster.

Continue reading...
title: Labour wins decisive victory in Greater Manchester mayoral byelection

author: Associated Press
description:
Sean Grayson, diagnosed with colon cancer, was sentenced to 20 years for killing Massey in Springfield in 2024

A former Illinois sheriff’s deputy won’t get an early medical release from his two-decade prison sentence for killing Sonya Massey inside her home after the Black woman called 911 about a possible prowler, state officials decided on Friday.

Sean Grayson had been diagnosed with colon cancer prior to the 2024 shooting, and his attorney noted in January that the cancer had advanced to his liver and lungs.

Continue reading...
title: Illinois officer who killed Sonya Massey denied medical release from prison

author: Edward Helmore
description:
Body of William Standish discovered in Teton mountains as investigators say fatal fall likely cause of death

A 28-year-old Australian hiker who lost contact with his family while hiking the Continental Divide Trail between Yellowstone and Grand Teton national parks in Wyoming has been found dead, according to authorities.

The man, identified as William Standish, was discovered by rescuers on Wednesday morning in the Wigwams, a series of rocky peaks on the west slope of the Teton mountain range, the Teton county coroner said. Investigators say it was likely he suffered a fatal fall.

Continue reading...
title: Missing Australian hiker found dead in Wyoming, officials say

author: Associated Press
description:
Defense lawyers say Clancy was ill with postpartum psychosis when she killed three children in January 2023

Jurors walked through the Massachusetts home where Lindsay Clancy strangled her three children, a rare visit on Friday that let them see first-hand the place where an outwardly ordinary family life unraveled into tragedy.

After being driven past two businesses relevant to the narrative of the January 2023 killings, jurors were escorted in groups of six to view the inside of the house, including the basement where the children died.

In the US, you can call or text the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline at 988 or chat at 988lifeline.org. In the UK and Ireland, Samaritans can be contacted on freephone 116 123. In Australia, the crisis su
title: Jurors in Lindsay Clancy murder trial visit home where children were killed

author: Jessica Glenza
description:
Data by one test-maker shows a positivity drop, but rate could be influenced by number of people taking test

  • Sign up for the Breaking News US newsletter email

The maker of a popular laboratory test said the cyclosporiasis outbreak in the US may be slowing. An outbreak of infections from the single-celled parasite has grown to more than 18,000 suspected and confirmed cases in late July, the nation’s largest on record.

The midwest has been hit particularly hard in the outbreak, where public health officials have linked infections in nine states to iceberg lettuce from Taylor Farms’ Mexico operations
title: Is the cyclosporiasis outbreak slowing? Test-makers are hopeful

author: Gabrielle Canon and agencies
description:
Federal government plan outlines cuts to California, Arizona and Nevada but fix is likely to be only temporary

The US government released its anxiously awaited plan for how to manage the Colorado river crisis on Friday, outlining cuts in water supplied to California, Arizona and Nevada.

The proposal from the US Bureau of Reclamation spares Colorado, Utah, New Mexico and Wyoming from facing mandatory cuts, for now. But it is a temporary fix as the states that rely on the river continue to fight over a long-term management plan for the dwindling resource that supplies huge swaths of the western US.

Continue reading...
title: Water cuts loom as US unveils long-awaited response to Colorado river crisis

author: Ben Beaumont-Thomas
description:
Duetting stars surpass record set in 1953, when crooner Frankie Laine hit the top with I Believe

Sam Fender and Olivia Dean have scored the longest running UK No 1 single in history with Rein Me In, beating a record that has stood since 1953.

Back then, the UK singles chart had been running for less than a year and contained just 12 songs when I Believe, a bombastic ballad by US crooner Frankie Laine, hit No 1 and spent a total of 18 weeks on the chart.

Continue reading...
title: Sam Fender and Olivia Dean’s Rein Me In breaks 73-year record to become longest-running UK No 1 single

author: Presented by Lucy Hough with Julian Borger; produced by Annie La Vespa and Angus Neale; senior producer Ryan Ramgobin
description:
Donald Trump has declared a breakthrough in negotiations over the disarmament of Hamas in Gaza and the withdrawal of Israeli forces, but Israeli government officials have voiced scepticism over the deal.

Lucy Hough speaks to Julian Borger, the Guardian’s senior international correspondent – watch on YouTube

Continue reading...
title: Hamas agrees to Trump’s plan to disarm in Gaza – The Latest

author: Simon Goodley
description:
Multimillionaire Peter Waddell is also found to have been properly dismissed from Big Motoring World for gross misconduct

A multimillionaire used-car salesman was ousted from his £300m company after “a pre-conceived and orchestrated plan” devised by private equity investors that had backed his business, a high court judge has ruled.

Peter Waddell, 60, was forced out as the chief executive of the Kent-based dealership Big Motoring World in 2024 in a coup that resulted in “more-or-less open warfare” at the car seller and caused “unfair prejudice” to the investment company that held Waddell’s majority stake.

Continue reading...
title: Boss of £300m used-car firm was ousted after ‘orchestrated plan’ by investors, judge rules

author: Achol Arok
description:
Ombudsman finds Homes NSW acted unreasonably and recommended additional payment for distress and suffering

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

An elderly public housing tenant whose home was damaged by sewage overflows will be fully compensated by the New South Wales government after it disposed of her personal belongings without her consent and failed to properly support her insurance claim.

The NSW Ombudsman on Friday published its report after an investigation in which it found Homes NSW acted unreasonably in how it handled the tenant’s contaminated belongings and “failed to provide full and accurate information to the insurer”.
title: NSW should compensate elderly woman whose public housing was inundated with sewage, ombudsman finds

author: Andy Vasoyan with visuals by Rajah Bose
description:
The handcrafted leather boots are a century-old tradition – but with money tight, the cost of up to $800 is harder to justify

For 18 years, one of the most important relationships in Luke Mayfield’s life was with his boots. As a hotshot – one of the US’s elite firefighting crews sent deep, on foot, into wildfires – Mayfield hiked a thousand miles a fire season in his boots, stood in them 16 hours a day and slept near them on assignments that lasted weeks in terrain no truck could reach.

Like every wildland firefighter, he learned the rituals of their upkeep: how to grease them, how to lace them, how soon before the season to break in a new pair so the blisters came during training instead of on duty.

Continue reading...
title: These boots are the safest for US wildland firefighters. Fewer and fewer can afford them

author: Joseph Gedeon in Washington
description:
President calls for former personal defense lawyer to be ‘immediately approved’ as attorney general

Donald Trump has defended controversial plans for a $1.8bn slush fund even as they threaten to derail the nomination of his former personal lawyer Todd Blanche for US attorney general.

Blanche “should be immediately approved” by the US Senate, the president declared in a post on his Truth Social platform on Friday morning, defending the payout scheme proposed by his officials in the Department of Justice as it holds up Blanche’s confirmation.

Continue reading...
title: Trump defends $1.8bn slush fund that is holding up Todd Blanche confirmation

author: Richard Luscombe
description:
Kaohly Her is accused of inappropriate conduct and creating a ‘sexualized work environment’ by senior officials

  • US politics live – latest updates

A second senior police official in St Paul has alleged sexual harassment and inappropriate conduct by the Minnesota city’s Democratic mayor, Kaohly Her, following confirmation that an inquiry into her behavior was launched earlier this year.

The new claims were reported on Thursday by the Minnesota Star Tribune, which said it obtained further details of the mayor’s alleged actions that gave rise to the original complaint b
title: Second police official in St Paul alleges sexual harassment by mayor

author: Richard Luscombe
description:
Move seeking $3.25m in damages six months after mother of Today show host Savannah Guthrie was last seen safe

Two men questioned early in the search for NBC’s Today Show host Savannah Guthrie’s missing mother said they will file a $3.25m wrongful arrest lawsuit against the sheriff who detained them, as the investigation passes the six-month mark this weekend.

Nancy Guthrie, 84, was last seen safe while at her Tucson, Arizona, home on 1 February. Authorities, including the FBI, believe she was kidnapped. But despite a number of leads and blood spatters at the house, no further trace of her has been found, and no suspects have emerged.

Continue reading...
title: Two men to file wrongful arrest lawsuit over Nancy Guthrie disappearance case

author: Josh Halliday North of England editor
description:
UK prime minister is the first head of a major nation to call on the under-pressure Fifa president to step down

  • UK politics live – latest updates

Andy Burnham has called on the Fifa president, Gianni Infantino, to resign over his “outrageous” plans to sell a stake in the World Cup.

Infantino faces growing pressure over his proposals, which triggered a backlash among football bodies and prompted the resignation on Friday of a key adviser.

Continue reading...
title: Andy Burnham calls on Infantino to resign over ‘outrageous’ World Cup plans

author: Helena Horton
description:
Exclusive: Danielle Kirton calls on Ed Miliband to help her get answers about why evacuation order came too late

The bereaved daughter of a British couple who died in a Spanish wildfire is calling on Ed Miliband to get answers from Spain’s government about why her parents were not told to evacuate until it was too late.

Severe wildfires have burned across Spain and France since early July, killing people, destroying thousands of homes and forcing more than 300,000 people to flee.

Continue reading...
title: Daughter of British couple killed in Spanish wildfire rejects claim they ignored order to leave

author: Associated Press
description:
Scientists and sky gazers will watch intently as rocket’s upper stage slams into lunar surface on Wednesday

A drifting SpaceX rocket is on a collision course with the moon after launching a pair of lunar landers more than a year ago.

The rocket’s upper stage will unintentionally slam into the moon on Wednesday, carving out a crater and sending up a plume of dust and rubble that scientists – and sky gazers – are eager to observe.

Continue reading...
title: Drifting SpaceX rocket heading for accidental collision with moon

author: Zoe Wood
description:
Average pump price reaches 160p a litre, while diesel is up 14.5p to 179p and forecast to go to 185p soon

  • Business live – latest updates

The price of petrol has hit a new Iran War high at UK forecourts, adding to the financial pressure on millions of households about to embark on their annual holiday.

The RAC said that in “very unwelcome news for drivers” the average pump price had reached 160p a litre, reversing the drop down to 151p in early July that followed the announcement of a fragile Middle East ceasefire.
title: UK petrol price hits Iran war high, adding to pressure on households

author: Priya Bharadia
description:
More than 80 loved ones spoke of horrors of learning about Robert Bush’s crimes, including mother of a miscarried baby

A funeral director has been jailed for 20 years for leaving dozens of bodies – including a miscarried baby – “rotting” in his mortuary and giving bereaved families the wrong ashes.

Robert Bush, the owner of Legacy Independent Funeral Services in Hull, pleaded guilty to 67 offences spanning 12 years and affecting hundreds of families, including 30 counts of preventing a lawful and decent burial.

Continue reading...
title: Hull funeral director who left bodies to rot in mortuary jailed for 20 years

author: Nicola Slawson
description:
Senators Warren and Van Hollen attack Republican ‘rubber stamps’ in Congress for surrendering authority to Trump. Plus, could AI take your job? Some workers in China already know the answer

Good morning.

Senior Democrats accused Republicans in the US Congress of becoming “gelatinous blobs” who will not stand up to Donald Trump and “rubber stamps” for his war on Iran.

What else is happening in Washington? Trump has said a deal has been reached for Hamas to disarm and for Israel to withdraw its forces from Gaza. However, briefings from both sides exposed disputes over its implementation that could prove difficult to overcome.

What has Blanche said? Blanche has already said publicly that the payout fund to compensate
title: Top Democrats accuse Republicans of becoming ‘gelatinous blobs’ on Iran war | First Thing

author: Rachel Leingang
description:
President grapples with finding a resolution to Middle East conflict that has pushed up gasoline prices ahead of vital midterm elections

  • Sign up for the US Breaking News email

Hello and welcome to the US politics live blog.

President Donald Trump will convene a cabinet meeting later today at his ⁠Camp David retreat as he grapples with how to resolve his war against Iran.

President Donald Trump has said he may pull Todd Blanche’s nomination for attorney-general until senators John Cornyn and Thom Tillis leave office. The Republicans have demanded written assurances about the settlement of the presiden
title: Trump to meet cabinet at Camp David as Iran war drags on – US politics live

author: Oliver Milman
description:
Contender, largest tagged male great white, heading north as overheating oceans alter range of several shark species

The largest tagged male great white shark in the Atlantic Ocean has been identified traveling up the US and Canada coastline amid a surge in sightings of sharks that are increasingly shifting their movement patterns due to the overheating of the oceans.

The great white shark, named Contender, is nearly 14ft long and weighs more than 1,650lbs. The hulking fish has been pinged in several locations off North Carolina and Maine as he headed north for the summer, with Contender’s last known location located off Nova Scotia in Canada on 11 July.

Continue reading...
title: Huge great white spotted traveling up US and Canada as shark sightings surge

author: PA Media
description:
The Royal Mint Court residents’ association tried to fight decision to grant planning permission

  • UK politics live – latest updates

Construction of a new Chinese super embassy in London can go ahead after the high court dismissed a challenge to the government’s decision to grant planning permission.

The Royal Mint Court residents’ association (RMCRA) brought legal action against the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government, and the London borough of Tower Hamlets.

Continue reading...
title: Chinese super embassy in London to go ahead after high court challenge dismissed

author: Heather Timmons
description:
Ben Cohen says his ice cream company has been silenced by corporate ownership – and a boycott of Magnum brands could force a sale

Ben & Jerry’s ice cream in the tub is still great, but the brand’s newest chocolate-covered ice cream bar on a stick?

“It ain’t the same,” Ben Cohen, the company co-founder, told the Guardian. Sure, the chocolate coating is still thick enough, but the ice cream itself is “kinda fluffy”, Cohen said – an insult in the ice cream world that suggests extra air was added to cut costs.

Continue reading...
title: ‘It ain’t the same’: inside the bitter battle to free Ben & Jerry’s

author: Joanna Partridge and Sarah Butler
description:
Trio set up Swift Partners for the acquisition, allowing supermarket to focus on core food business

Sainsbury’s has agreed to sell the Argos retail chain for £120m to allow it to concentrate on its core food business.

The supermarket announced on Friday it was selling the catalogue shopping business to a trio of retail veterans, a decade after buying the company for more than £1bn.

Continue reading...
title: Sainsbury’s to sell Argos to three retail veterans in £120m deal

author: Jillian Ambrose Energy correspondent
description:
Boom in solar farms and home installations in first half of 2026 began shortly after start of US-Israel war against Iran

Great Britain has recorded more new solar power installations in the first half of this year than in any six-month period since 2011, as households turn to rooftop panels to help cut their energy bills.

An analysis of the government’s official figures shows that Great Britain added 142,536 solar installations in the first six months of the year, putting it on track to top last year’s record solar additions.

Continue reading...
title: New solar panels in Great Britain at 15-year high as fossil fuel costs soar

author: Guardian staff and agencies
description:
Some drowned and others caught up in crush, official says, and thousands sleep on streets or in parks

At least 18 people have died trying to reach the Spanish enclave of Ceuta after about 49,000 migrants breached the border with Morocco and poured into the tiny territory.

Spain sent ​military and police reinforcements to Ceuta on Thursday after people crossed by land and sea. Spain’s prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, is expected to join the interior minister, Fernando Grande-Marlaska, on a visit to Ceuta on Friday morning.

Continue reading...
title: At least 18 die trying to cross to Spanish enclave of Ceuta from Morocco

author: Jasper Jolly
description:
Live, rolling coverage as British oil company looks for buyer amid political dispute over future drilling licences

Another of the top risers on the FTSE 100 this morning is Sainsbury’s. The supermarket chain is up 4% after it said it had agreed the £120m sale of catalogue shopping business Argos to a trio of retail veterans – a decade after buying the company for more than £1bn.

Sainsbury’s said it would be able to fully focus on its core food business and “creating a simpler business with higher margins, higher growth and stronger free cash flow generation”.

What attracted us to Argos is the strength of the business, with a trusted brand, loyal customers and dedicated colleagues. We believe strongly in Argos’s future and see real opportunities to invest and build on its progress.

Argos’s combination - of a strong digital business supported by standalone stores, stores inside Sainsbury’s and local fulfilment
title: BP to sell North Sea business; AI companies lead record surge on Korea’s stock market – business live

author: Joanna Partridge
description:
Price of an average home now £277,542, up from £277,484 the previous month but lower than in May, says Nationwide

  • Business live – latest updates

Economic uncertainty dampened UK house price growth in July as prospective house buyers remained cautious about interest rates during the US war with Iran in what should be peak housebuying season.

House prices rose by just 0.1% in July from a month earlier, according to the lender Nationwide, while annual price growth slowed to 1.8% this month, down from 2.2% in June.

Continue reading...
title: UK house prices up 0.1% in July as buyers remain cautious on interest rates

author: Caroline Davies
description:
More than 100 firefighters remain at scene after Dunwich Heath blaze spread across 150 hectares and forced evacuations

Fire crews tackling a large wildfire burning for more than 24 hours near Britain’s biggest nuclear power station have said the situation is “stabilising”.

More than 100 firefighters have been battling the blaze in Dunwich Heath, near Leiston, on the Suffolk coast since Wednesday evening.

Continue reading...
title: Suffolk wildfire near Sizewell nuclear plant ‘stabilising’ after 24 hours

author: Caitlin Cassidy
description:
Hancock Prospecting says chair Kim Williams among those ‘on notice’ for failing to remove program that joked about turning Rinehart’s insides into a sausage roll

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Gina Rinehart has threatened the ABC with legal action over crude comments aired on the national broadcaster, including a joke about mixing her guts into a sausage roll.

The four-minute film, titled A Very Relaxing Video, aired on the Race Around the World program on 12 July and concluded with the film-maker, Kate McGuinness, making crude and offensive comments about Rinehart.

Cont
title: Gina Rinehart threatens ABC with legal action over Race Around the World program

author: Guardian staff
description:
Move, which will end six decades of production in area, comes as new CEO tries to simplify firm and cut debt

  • Business live – latest updates

BP has put its North Sea oil and gas business up for sale, as it looks to end six decades of production from the region.

The oil major announced on Friday morning that it had launched a formal process to market its North Sea business for a potential sale. The move comes as BP’s new chief executive, Meg O’Neill, tries to simplify the company and cut its debt levels.

Continue reading...
title: BP puts North Sea oil and gas business up for sale

author: Penry Buckley
description:
Robert Assaf separately tells anti-corruption inquiry money funnelled through lobbying firm to create ‘maximum benefit from a tax perspective’

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A group of young conservative Liberal power brokers accused of soliciting illegal donations used some of the funds to pay for a bucks night, one of its members has told a corruption inquiry.

The
title: ‘Rob has the bucks cash’: NSW Liberals used Reformers funds to pay for ‘personal expenditure’, Icac hears

author: Denis Campbell Health policy editor
description:
Scheme brought in up to 500 foreign-trained doctors a year and was seen as example of British ‘soft power’

The NHS has scrapped a longstanding scheme that let overseas doctors boost their skills in UK hospitals and was seen as an example of British “soft power”.

Senior doctors have criticised NHS England’s decision to axe the Medical Training Initiative, under which 400 to 500 foreign-trained doctors were given placements in Britain every year.

Continue reading...
title: Medical colleges condemn scrapping of NHS placements for overseas doctors

author: Geraldine McKelvie Senior correspondent
description:
She Plays to Win face losing one of their female players after being told team must include a male

The UK’s only all-female chess team have been promoted to the game’s top tier – only to be told they will have to add a man to their squad.

She Plays to Win Lionesses A Team have fallen foul of a rule designed to boost female participation in the sport.

Continue reading...
title: Fury as UK’s only all-female chess team promoted – then told they must recruit a man

author: Tom McIlroy and Krishani Dhanji
description:
Exclusive: ADF personnel who were discriminated against for being LGBTQ+ are owed a national apology, federal government told

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A national apology should be issued to LGBTQ+ veterans and service personnel who experienced discrimin
title: Forced out of Australia’s military due to his sexuality, David says an apology is ‘long overdue’ for veterans like him

author: Michael Segalov
description:
In today’s newsletter: ​The legal protections once considered foundational ​in conflict are now routinely bypassed​,​ with healthcare personnel treated as legitimate targets

Good morning. While you were asleep, Donald Trump claimed a deal had been reached for the “complete disarmament of Hamas” in Gaza. His announcement, characteristically, does not yet seem watertight, with briefings from both sides revealing points of contention, and as such is being treated with caution by some world leaders.

As anyone paying attention knows, the conflict has seen Israel and Hamas accused of war crimes, and two years ago, the international criminal court issued an arrest warrant for Benjamin Netanyahu. Elsewhere in the region, the Israel-US military operation in Iran has been
title: Friday briefing: Why attacks on hospitals from Ukraine to Lebanon now happen with impunity

description:
Response from Hamas and Israeli officials suggest Gaza deal still faces obstacles; Tehran launches drone strikes at Kuwait in retaliation for recent US attacks

  • Trump claims agreement for ‘complete disarmament’ of Hamas in Gaza but support uncertain

  • Saudi Arabia prepares sea and possible land offensive against Houthis

Donald Trump claims a deal has been reached for Hamas to disarm and Israel to withdraw its forces from Gaza, but many hurdles and conditions remained in the Palestinian territory.

“The agreement will be carried out in carefully structured phases,” Trump said on social media. “As disarmament is completed, Israeli forces will withdraw, and the Intern
title: Middle East crisis live: Trump claims Gaza deal reached; Iran targets US bases in Kuwait

author: Jonathan Barrett Business editor
description:
London-based company to sell local loan portfolio to Blackstone but will continue private and institutional banking services

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The London-headquartered HSBC is closing all Australian branches over the next 18 months after selling its local mortgage and personal loan portfolio to the global asset giant Blackstone.

The transaction will end HSBC’s
title: HSBC to pull out of Australian retail banking market

author: Australian Associated Press
description:
Andrés Felipe Valencia Barrientos found guilty of two counts of assault and not guilty of three of six counts of rape

A British musician and YouTube personality on trial for allegedly violently raping a fan in a Perth hotel has been acquitted of three sexual penetration charges.

But the jury found the rapper Yung Filly guilty of two assault offences related to his September 2024 encounter with a 20-year-old woman after a show.

Continue reading...
title: British YouTuber Yung Filly acquitted of raping fan in Perth but could face retrial with jury hung on three charges

author: Benita Kolovos Victorian state correspondent
description:
Geoffrey Watson criticises Victorian government as union administrator warns of ongoing criminality on construction sites

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Integrity expert Geoffrey Watson SC says “nobody” from the Victorian Labor government has contacted him about his bombshell report alleging corruption in the construction union which he estimated
title: ‘Nobody from the Labor party has contacted me’ about $15bn CFMEU corruption claim, expert says

author: Presented by Jonathan Freedland with Bhaskar Sunkara, produced by May Robson and Nada Smiljanic; the executive producer is Maz Ebtehaj
description:
Leftwing Democrats are having their moment in the sun, with Zohran Mamdani in New York, Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan and endless calls for Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez to run for president in 2028. Has Democratic socialism shifted from the political fringe to the mainstream? And can this group lure back the all-important swing voters?

Jonathan Freedland speaks to Bhaskar Sunkara, president of the Nation magazine, founding editor of Jacobin and author of The Socialist Manifesto: The Case for Radical Politics in an Era of Extreme Inequalities

author: Ima Caldwell
description:
Queensland police fine driver of another car that allegedly caused Yaris to swerve before it hit kerb and catapulted into air – and bus

A Queensland driver has been fined after being involved in a stunning crash that saw a car become airborne and then stuck in the side of a bus.

The drama unfolded at Rocklea in Brisbane’s south on Wednesday evening. A blue Toyota Yaris hit a traffic island and was catapulted into the air before smashing into the side of the council bus. The back of the car was left protruding from the bus.

Continue reading...
title: ‘A car in the bus!’: Toyota becomes airborne and then wedges in side of Brisbane bus

author: Krishani Dhanji
description:
One Nation leader’s ‘how can you tell me there are good Muslims?’ remarks were the subject of complaints, but police say the matter has now been finalised

The Australian federal police has determined One Nation leader Pauline Hanson’s comments about Muslim Australians “do not meet the threshold” of breaching hate laws.

The AFP said it received several complaints about Hanson’s remarks to Sky News on 16 February.

Continue reading...
title: Pauline Hanson’s comments on ‘good Muslims’ don’t breach hate speech laws, Australian federal police finds

author: Reuters
description:
US president’s board of peace says Israel will withdraw from Gaza following disarmament of Hamas but no immediate statement from either side

  • What is Trump’s Board of Peace and who is involved?

Donald Trump on Thursday announced an agreement for the “complete disarmament” of Hamas, calling it a critical step toward a new Palestinian government in Gaza. There was no immediate statement from Hamas or Israel on the agreement.

“This agreement is a critical step towards Gaza finally being governed by a new Palestinian government that will work closely with the Board of Peace to help the Palestinian people,” Trump said in a social media post.

Continue reading...
title: Trump claims agreement for ‘complete disarmament’ of Hamas in Gaza but support uncertain

author: Reuters
description:
Company says it discovered unauthorized access during ‘proactive review’ after rival OpenAI revealed rogue agent

Anthropic ⁠said on Thursday its AI Claude model hacked ⁠systems of ⁠three ​organizations during testing, days after rival OpenAI ⁠revealed a rogue agent had gone on a days-long ⁠hacking spree at AI ​firm Hugging ‌Face.

Claude gained ‌unauthorized access to the ‌systems during cybersecurity evaluations after a misconfiguration allowed the models to reach the internet from testing environments that ‌were supposed to be isolated, Anthropic said.

Continue reading...
title: Anthropic’s AI Claude escaped testing environment and hacked organizations
